summary: This sermon on James 1:26–2:13 argues that discrimination—treating people differently based on external factors like wealth, race, or status—exposes a fundamental contradiction in the Christian life. The preacher contends that showing favoritism reveals we are valuing earthly rewards over kingdom values, living for the wrong kingdom, and hypocritically judging others by the law while claiming grace for ourselves.
key_points: Discrimination reveals we value what people can do for us rather than their intrinsic worth
The kingdom of God is built on mercy and faith, not external status or power
We judge ourselves by grace but judge others by law—a hypocritical contradiction
Biblical love means inconveniencing yourself for others, especially those who cannot repay
Mercy triumphs over judgment; we are called to extend the grace we have received
big_idea: How we treat others—especially those who bring nothing to the table—reveals whether we truly live by the gospel of grace or are merely moral religious people building earthly kingdoms through discrimination.
title: Christian Contradictions
